questions.stem: A client on lithium has a level of 2.1, a coarse tremor, and vomiting. What is most likely?
questions.explanation: B is correct: a level of 2.1 is above the therapeutic range of about 0.8 to 1.2, and a coarse tremor with vomiting are toxicity signs. A dismisses a toxic level. C, serotonin syndrome, comes from serotonin drugs such as antidepressants, not lithium. D, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, comes from antipsychotics and shows high fever and rigid muscles.

questions.stem: For the client with lithium toxicity, what should the nurse do?

options.text: Hold the next dose, notify the provider, expect a repeat level and sodium check

questions.explanation: B is correct: hold the next dose, notify the provider, and expect a repeat level and sodium check. A continues the drug. C, low salt, raises lithium. D, less fluid, also raises the level.

questions.stem: Which client teaching about lithium is correct?

options.text: Keep salt and fluid intake steady, about 2 to 3 liters a day
Drink as little water as possible

questions.explanation: B is correct: low sodium or dehydration raises the level, so teach steady salt and fluid, about 2 to 3 liters a day. A and C raise the level. D is wrong because the safe range is narrow.

questions.stem: A client on an antipsychotic has a high fever and very rigid muscles. What is this?
questions.explanation: B is correct: high fever and very rigid muscles on an antipsychotic are neuroleptic malignant syndrome, an emergency. A involves agitation, sweating, and twitchy muscles. C is restlessness. D involves lithium.

questions.stem: A client takes two antidepressants. Which findings suggest serotonin syndrome? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: these are the taught signs of serotonin syndrome. E, lip smacking, is tardive dyskinesia.

questions.stem: A client develops neuroleptic malignant syndrome. What is the priority action?

options.text: Continue the drug and give a fever reducer
Stop the drug and notify the provider right away

questions.explanation: B is correct: both dangerous reactions are emergencies, so stop the drug and notify the provider right away. A and D continue the drug. C delays.

questions.stem: A client on an antipsychotic has lip smacking and tongue movements. Why should this be reported early?
questions.explanation: B is correct: lip smacking and tongue movements are tardive dyskinesia, which can be permanent, so report it early. A and D downplay it. C is unrelated.

questions.stem: A client on an antipsychotic can't sit still and keeps pacing. What is this called?
questions.explanation: B is correct: akathisia is restlessness, can't sit still. A is a sudden muscle spasm in the neck or eyes. C is lip smacking and tongue movements. D involves fever and twitchy muscles.

questions.stem: A client says, "I just don't want to be here anymore." What is the best response?
questions.explanation: B is correct: asking directly does not put the idea in the client's head; it opens the door to safety. A is false reassurance. C is a why question, which blocks communication. D changes the subject.

questions.stem: Which nurse statements are therapeutic? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A and B are correct: an open question and naming a feeling help. C is a why question, D is false reassurance, and E gives advice; all block communication.
